Description: Blocking zoom stops low-vision users from enlarging content on a phone, and fails resize text.
Do: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and nothing that caps the scale.
Don't: Add user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1.

Description: Toasts, 'item added' notes and result counts appear without moving focus, so a screen reader says nothing unless the region is live.
Do: Render messages into an existing role='status' (polite) or role='alert' (urgent) container.
Don't: Inject a new element with the text and expect it to be read.

Description: If the visuals carry information not in the speech, blind users miss it. Describe it in a separate audio track or the narration.
Do: Narrate on-screen actions in the script or add a described version.
Don't: Show steps visually with silent narration.

Issue: Autoplaying Audio Has a Stop Control
Description: Sound that plays for more than three seconds fights with screen reader speech. Users need to pause it or set its volume separately.
Do: Do not autoplay audio; if you must, give an immediate pause control near the top of the page.
Don't: Autoplay a video with sound.

Description: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users, and anyone watching muted on a train, rely on captions for the speech and meaningful sounds in a video.
Do: Add a WebVTT track with accurate captions and set default for the main language.
Don't: Rely on auto-generated captions without review, or burn them in with no track.

Issue: Colour Is Never the Only Signal
Description: Roughly one in twelve men has a colour vision difference. Red and green alone cannot tell them what failed or what passed.
Do: Pair colour with an icon, text label, pattern or underline.
Don't: Mark errors by turning a border red and nothing else.

Description: Phone numbers, chat widgets and contact links should sit in the same place on every page, so people who struggle can find help quickly.
Do: Keep the help link or number in the same header or footer position on all pages.
Don't: Move the contact route around by page type.
Code Example Bad: /* phone in header on home, footer on others */

Description: Menus that reorder themselves from page to page force people to relearn the site every click. Repeated navigation should keep its relative order.
Do: Render the same header and footer links in the same order on every page.
Don't: Reorder or hide primary links per page without reason.

Description: A screen reader announces a cell's row and column headers only when the table marks them with th and scope. Without them a grid of numbers is meaningless.
Do: Use th with scope, a caption, and keep layout out of tables.
Don't: Style td cells to look like headers.

Description: Screen readers pick a pronunciation engine from the lang attribute, and browsers use it for hyphenation, quotes and translation prompts.
Do: Set lang on the html element to the real language, with region where it matters.
Don't: Leave lang off or copy en from a template onto a page written in another language.

Description: Pure decoration read aloud is noise. An empty alt attribute tells assistive tech to skip the image.
Do: Use alt='' on decoration, or set it as a CSS background.
Don't: Omit alt entirely, which makes some readers announce the file name.

Description: Some people mount a tablet in one fixed orientation. Forcing portrait or landscape makes the app unusable for them unless the order is essential.
Do: Support both orientations and test layouts rotated.
Don't: Lock the screen to one orientation by default.

Description: Sortable lists, sliders and file drop zones that only work by dragging exclude many users. Provide a click or keyboard path to the same result.
Do: Offer move up and move down buttons, or a select-then-place flow.
Don't: Allow reordering with drag only.

Issue: Enhanced Contrast Where It Is Cheap
Description: The AAA level asks for 7:1 for body text. Long-form reading, older audiences and outdoor use benefit from it.
Do: Aim for 7:1 on body text on content-heavy and care or public service sites.
Don't: Stop at the bare minimum on long reading pages.

Description: Keyboard navigation must reach every action a mouse can: Tab, Enter, Space and arrow keys. Clickable divs are invisible to the keyboard and to assistive tech.
Do: Use button for actions and a for navigation; they bring focus, Enter and Space handling for free.
Don't: Attach click handlers to div or span and add role and key handlers by hand.

Description: Moving focus onto a field must not submit, navigate or open a new window. Surprises disorient screen reader and keyboard users.
Do: Change context only on explicit activation such as Enter or a click on a button.
Don't: Auto-submit when a field receives focus.

Issue: Focus Not Hidden Behind Sticky Bars
Description: A fixed header, cookie bar or chat bubble can cover the element that just received keyboard focus, so the user tabs into something they cannot see.
Do: Give the scroll container scroll-padding equal to the height of the fixed bars, and test by tabbing through the whole page.
Don't: Pin bars over content without reserving space for focused elements.

Description: The focus indicator is a user interface component state, so it needs at least 3:1 contrast against the neighbouring colours. A pale blue ring on white fails.
Do: Check the ring against both the page and the control it surrounds; use a two-tone ring (dark inner, light outer) on mixed backgrounds.
Don't: Pick a ring colour by eye on one background and assume it works on cards, images and dark sections.

Description: Anyone using a keyboard, switch or voice control needs to see which control is active. A removed or invisible focus ring leaves them guessing where the next Enter press lands.
Do: Style :focus-visible with a 2px outline in a colour that holds 3:1 against the page and the control, offset a couple of pixels.
Don't: Remove the outline with outline:none unless a stronger replacement indicator is drawn in the same rule.

Description: Headings are a navigation list for assistive tech users. Levels should nest by meaning, not by font size.
Do: One h1 per page, h2 for sections, h3 beneath them; restyle with CSS to change the look.
Don't: Pick h4 because it looks smaller, or skip from h1 to h4.

Description: Headings and form labels should say what the section or field is. Vague ones make skimming with assistive tech slow.
Do: Write headings that describe their section and labels that name the field.
Don't: Use 'Details' or 'Info' for every heading.

Issue: Hover and Focus Content Is Dismissible
Description: A tooltip or popover that appears on hover must be dismissible with Escape, stay put while the pointer moves onto it, and remain until the user is done.
Do: Let Escape close it, keep it open while hovered or focused, and show it on keyboard focus too.
Don't: Show a tooltip only on mouse hover and remove it the moment the pointer drifts.

Description: A button that shows just an icon has no accessible name unless you supply one. Voice-control users also need a name they can say.
Do: Add visible text, or aria-label that matches what sighted users infer; hide the svg itself from the tree.
Don't: Ship an icon button with no text or label.

Description: An icon or label that means search in one place should not mean filter in another.
Do: Use one icon and one name per function across the site.
Don't: Rename or redraw the same control on different pages.

Description: An image that carries meaning needs a text equivalent that gives the same information, not a description of its pixels.
Do: Write alt for the purpose: what the reader would miss without it. Keep it a phrase or a sentence.
Don't: Start with 'image of', paste a filename, or stuff keywords.

Description: Changing a select or radio should not move the user to another page unless they were told it would.
Do: Add an explicit Go button, or state the behaviour before the control.
Don't: Navigate in a select's change handler.

Issue: Instructions Do Not Rely on Shape or Position
Description: 'Press the round button on the right' means nothing to someone who cannot see the layout.
Do: Refer to controls by their visible label.
Don't: Describe controls by colour, shape or location only.
Code Example Bad: Press the green button on the right.

Description: Unrequested pop-ups and notifications interrupt focus and reading. Let people delay or suppress non-urgent ones.
Do: Batch non-urgent messages and offer a setting to defer them.
Don't: Open an offer modal while the user is mid-task.

Description: Screen reader users jump between landmarks to scan a page. Header, nav, main and footer elements expose that structure without extra attributes.
Do: Use one main, a nav per link group with a distinguishing label, and header and footer at page level.
Don't: Build the page from anonymous divs, or use two main elements.

Description: Screen reader users often pull up a list of links. 'Click here' and 'Read more' repeated ten times is an unusable list.
Do: Make the link text meaningful alone, or add visually hidden text that completes it.
Don't: Repeat 'Read more' on every card.

Description: A passage in another language read with the page's voice is gibberish. A lang attribute on the span or block fixes the pronunciation.
Do: Wrap foreign phrases and quotations in an element with the matching lang value.
Don't: Leave a French or Welsh phrase inside English text with no marker.

Description: Pointer targets should be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or have enough spacing around smaller ones. Small close icons and tag buttons miss this most.
Do: Pad the hit area with min-width and min-height of 24px (44px for primary actions on touch).
Don't: Shrink icons to 14px with no padding.

Description: When a modal opens, focus must move into it, stay inside while it is open, and return to the trigger when it closes.
Do: Use dialog.showModal(), which traps focus and handles Escape, and restore focus to the opener on close.
Don't: Show a div over the page and leave focus behind it.

Issue: More Than One Way to Find Pages
Description: People find content differently: menu, search, sitemap, links. On sites with many pages, offering two or more routes helps.
Do: Provide navigation plus search or a sitemap link.
Don't: Rely on one hierarchical menu alone.

Description: In a single-page app, a route change does not reload the page, so focus and the screen reader cursor stay on the old link. Users hear nothing happen.
Do: After navigation, move focus to the new h1 or main and update the document title.
Don't: Swap the view and leave focus on the clicked link.

Description: Hiding a link or button from the accessibility tree while it can still take focus leaves keyboard users on a control that is announced as nothing.
Do: Use inert or hidden on whole off-screen panels so they leave both the tab order and the tree.
Don't: Set aria-hidden='true' on a container that holds links.

Description: Content that flashes more than three times in a second can trigger seizures. There is no safe visual style that does it.
Do: Keep any flashing below that threshold, and check video and GIF content before publishing.
Don't: Use strobe-style transitions or flashing alerts.

Description: If focus enters a widget such as an embedded player or editor, the user must be able to leave it with standard keys. A trap forces them to reload.
Do: Test every embed and custom widget by tabbing in and out; document Escape or a dedicated exit key when one is needed.
Don't: Capture Tab inside a component with no way out except the mouse.

Description: Borders of inputs, icons that carry meaning and chart marks must reach 3:1 against what is next to them, or people with low vision cannot find them.
Do: Give form field borders, toggles and meaningful icons a 3:1 edge or fill.
Don't: Use a 1px light grey border on a white form so the field fades away.

Description: Anything that moves for over five seconds beside other content, such as carousels, tickers and animated backgrounds, needs a visible way to pause it.
Do: Provide a real pause button and stop auto-advance on hover and focus.
Don't: Auto-rotate a hero with no controls.

Description: Pinch, multi-finger swipe and path drawing are hard or impossible for people using a stylus, head pointer or tremor. A tap-based alternative must exist.
Do: Add plus and minus buttons beside pinch-zoom and arrow buttons beside swipe.
Don't: Offer zoom or navigation only through a two-finger gesture.

Description: A custom control needs name, role and state exposed to assistive tech. Native button, select and input give that for free; ARIA only describes, it adds no behaviour.
Do: Reach for the native element first; add ARIA only for patterns HTML lacks, and follow the APG keyboard model.
Don't: Put role='button' on a div without tabindex, key handling and state.

Description: When a session expires and the user signs in again, the work they had should still be there.
Do: Persist form state in the session or local storage before redirecting to sign-in.
Don't: Redirect to login and drop the half-complete form.

Issue: Real Text, Not Images of Text
Description: Text rendered as an image will not resize, reflow, restyle or translate. Logos are the exception.
Do: Set text in HTML and style it with CSS.
Don't: Export headings or offers as banners.

Description: At 400 percent zoom a desktop window behaves like a 320px screen. Content must stack in one column without sideways scrolling, apart from maps, tables and similar two-dimensional content.
Do: Test at 320px width and at 400% zoom; use fluid grids and wrap long strings.
Don't: Set min-width on the page or wrapper bigger than a phone.

Description: Parallax, large slides and zooms can trigger dizziness or nausea for people with vestibular conditions. The operating system exposes a preference.
Do: Wrap large movement in a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference query, or replace it with a short fade.
Don't: Ignore the setting and animate everything.

Description: Firing on pointer-down gives no chance to cancel a slip. Letting the user slide off before release prevents accidental activation.
Do: Use click (fires on up) rather than mousedown or touchstart for actions.
Don't: Trigger purchases on mousedown.

Description: Long documents are easier to scan when sections are broken up with headings.
Do: Give each section its own heading.
Don't: Run a long article as one block.

Issue: Single-key Shortcuts Can Be Turned Off
Description: One-letter shortcuts collide with speech input, which can fire them while the user is dictating. They must be disableable or remappable, or only act when the component has focus.
Do: Scope shortcuts to the focused widget, or require a modifier key.
Don't: Bind bare letters at the window level.

Description: Keyboard users should not tab through twenty header links on every page. A skip link is the first focusable element and jumps past repeated blocks.
Do: Put an anchor to #main first in the body, visually hidden until focused, and give main that id.
Don't: Hide the skip link with display:none, which removes it from the tab order.

Description: A screen reader reads source order. If CSS places the price before the name visually but after it in the source, the sequence reads wrongly.
Do: Order the source as it should be read and use grid areas for placement.
Don't: Use order or absolute positioning to reverse content that depends on sequence.

Description: Some readers override line height, letter and word spacing. Content must remain readable with no clipped text when they do.
Do: Use unitless line-height and let boxes grow; test with a spacing bookmarklet.
Don't: Clip text with overflow:hidden in a box of set height.

Description: Keyboard users move through the DOM order. If the visual layout and the source order disagree, focus jumps around the screen in a way nobody predicts.
Do: Write the markup in the order people read it and let CSS grid or flex place it; leave tabindex at 0 or -1 only.
Don't: Use positive tabindex values or CSS order to reshuffle interactive elements.

Description: Podcasts and voice clips need a transcript so deaf users and anyone who cannot play sound can still read the content.
Do: Publish a transcript on the same page or one link away.
Don't: Offer only an audio player.

Description: Body text needs 4.5:1 against its background and large text (24px, or 19px bold) needs 3:1. Pale grey on white is the most common failure.
Do: Measure the real pair with a contrast tool, including text over images and on hover and disabled-looking states that still carry meaning.
Don't: Judge contrast by eye on a bright monitor, or put text straight on a photo.

Description: People enlarge text in the browser. Layouts built on fixed pixel heights clip or overlap once text doubles.
Do: Size type in rem and let containers grow with min-height, not height.
Don't: Fix heights in px on text containers, or block zoom.

Description: The title is the first thing a screen reader announces and the label on the browser tab and history. Identical titles make pages indistinguishable.
Do: Lead with the page's own subject, then the site name; update the title on every route change in a single-page app.
Don't: Ship one title for the whole site, or leave 'Untitled' or 'Home' on inner pages.

Description: Voice control users say what they see. If the aria-label differs from the visible text, the spoken command fails.
Do: Start the accessible name with the exact visible words.
Don't: Show 'Book now' and set aria-label to 'Reserve an appointment'.

Description: A form that silently expires costs people with slower input their work. Time limits need a warning and a way to extend.
Do: Warn at least 20 seconds ahead with a simple extend action, and save drafts.
Don't: Log the user out mid-form without notice.

Description: A thumbs rating with an optional reason improves quality and signals that the system can be wrong.
Do: Offer a quick rating and a free-text reason.
Don't: Hide the feedback path.

Description: Users should be able to correct their prompt, regenerate and undo applied changes.
Do: Provide edit, retry and revert for each result.
Don't: Apply changes irreversibly.

Description: People must know when text or images come from a model, and that it may be wrong.
Do: Label generated content and add a short reliability note near it.
Don't: Present generated text as human or authoritative.

Issue: Stream Responses With a Stop Control
Description: Streaming shows progress, but a stream that cannot be stopped traps users. Announce completion politely.
Do: Show a stop button and set aria-live='polite' on a finished-message region.
Don't: Stream with no way to cancel.

Description: Animating width, top or margin forces layout every frame. Transform and opacity stay on the compositor.
Do: Animate transform and opacity; avoid layout properties.
Don't: Animate height or left.

Description: The View Transitions API smooths changes between states or pages without hand-rolled clones.
Do: Wrap state updates in document.startViewTransition where supported, with a plain fallback.
Don't: Build manual clone-and-fly animations.

Description: Infinite pulses, spinners that never resolve and bouncing arrows pull attention from the task and burn battery.
Do: Run loops only while loading or live, stop them afterwards.
Don't: Pulse a fake 'live' dot or a bouncing chevron forever.

Description: Things entering the screen should decelerate; things leaving should accelerate. Linear motion feels mechanical.
Do: Use ease-out for entering, ease-in for leaving, ease-in-out for moves.
Don't: Use linear for UI movement.

Description: Interface feedback in the 150 to 250ms range feels immediate. Longer than about 400ms starts to feel like waiting.
Do: Use 150-250ms for hovers and toggles, up to 400ms for large panel moves.
Don't: Run 800ms transitions on routine controls.

Description: Flashing a spinner for 100ms feels worse than none. Show it only after a short delay and keep it up for a minimum time.
Do: Wait about 200ms before showing a spinner.
Don't: Flash it immediately.

Description: Animation that does not explain a change, such as a hero that drifts for no reason, is decoration and tires the eye.
Do: Animate to show cause and effect, orientation or state; remove anything that explains nothing.
Don't: Add movement to every element for polish.

Description: transition:all animates things you did not intend, such as layout changes on resize, and costs more.
Do: List only the properties that should move.
Don't: Use transition:all as a default.

Description: Layers moving at different speeds can cause motion sickness and cost scroll performance.
Do: Use subtle parallax on one element and disable under reduced motion.
Don't: Apply it to the whole page.

Description: Sections that fade up on scroll the same way every time slow reading and flag a template. Use reveals where order matters.
Do: Reveal only elements whose entrance explains something; keep content visible without script.
Don't: Fade and slide every section on enter.

Description: will-change reserves memory for each element. Applied broadly it slows pages down.
Do: Apply it shortly before an animation and remove after.
Don't: Add will-change to everything.

Description: If a user clicks again mid-animation and the UI waits, it feels laggy or lands in the wrong state.
Do: Use CSS transitions that reverse smoothly, or cancel running animations.
Don't: Block input until the animation ends.

Description: 'Submit' and 'Get started' tell people little. A verb plus object states the result.
Do: Label with verb and object: Book a visit, Get a quote.
Don't: Use 'Click here' or 'Learn more' everywhere.

Description: 04/05/26 means different days to different readers. Spell out the month and use the user's locale.
Do: Format with Intl.DateTimeFormat and include the month name.
Don't: Use all-numeric ambiguous dates.

Description: 1234567 is hard to read and a price without a currency is ambiguous. Intl.NumberFormat handles grouping and symbols.
Do: Format with Intl.NumberFormat and the right currency code.
Don't: Show raw floats like 19.9.

Description: Made-up testimonials, ratings and statistics destroy trust and may break advertising law. Every figure comes from the owner and can be checked.
Do: Use real, named quotes and numbers with a source; drop the row if none exist.
Don't: Invent reviews or counts.

Description: Lorem ipsum, 'Your title here' and stock names reach live pages more often than anyone admits. Real content shapes the design.
Do: Write real copy first; fail the build on known placeholders.
Don't: Leave filler text in sections.

Description: Short sentences and common words help everyone, and are essential for readers with cognitive or language difficulties.
Do: Aim for a lower secondary reading level and define jargon.
Don't: Fill pages with buzzwords such as seamless or elevate.
Code Example Good: We fix boilers the same day.

Description: Stock photos of people at laptops tell visitors nothing. Photos of the real team, work and premises build recognition.
Do: Use photos of the actual business with meaningful alt text.
Don't: Use generic stock imagery.

Issue: Truncate With Access to the Full Text
Description: Ellipses hide names, addresses and prices. If the cut hides something needed, provide it in full elsewhere.
Do: Truncate decoration only; wrap essential text, or reveal it on expand.
Don't: Cut a price or address with an ellipsis.

Issue: Bulk Actions Are Reversible and Counted
Description: Selecting many rows and applying an action is risky. Show the count and allow undo.
Do: Display '12 selected' and confirm with the number.
Don't: Apply to hidden pages silently.

Description: A calendar-only picker is slow for birth dates and tiring for keyboard users. Let people type the date.
Do: Accept typed dates with a clear format and show a calendar as an extra.
Don't: Force clicking through years.

Description: A column header that sorts needs a button inside and aria-sort for state.
Do: Put a button in th and set aria-sort.
Don't: Make the th click only.

Description: 'Done' is vague. State what happened and what comes next, such as when to expect a call.
Do: Say what was saved, sent or booked, with a time or reference.
Don't: Show a generic checkmark.
Code Example Good: Booked for Tue 12 May, 9:30. We will text a reminder.

Issue: Empty States Say What to Do
Description: An empty list is a chance to explain and offer a first step, in plain words.
Do: Say what belongs here and give one action to add it.
Don't: Leave an empty box or write 'No data'.
Code Example Good: No bookings yet. Add the first one

Description: 'Failed to load' leaves people stranded. Tell them what happened and offer retry, a different route or contact details.
Do: Name the problem, show a retry button and keep their work.
Don't: Show a stack trace or a dead end.

Description: A skeleton in the shape of the content gives structure while it loads and avoids layout jumps; a lone spinner gives nothing.
Do: Use skeletons for content areas and spinners only for short, unknown waits under a second.
Don't: Show a blank page until everything arrives.

Description: Phones lose signal. Telling people the app is offline and what still works beats silent failures.
Do: Listen for the offline event and show a banner; queue writes where possible.
Don't: Let requests fail without a message.

Description: Showing the result at once feels fast, but if the server refuses, the user must be told and the view restored.
Do: Update the UI, and on failure revert and explain.
Don't: Update optimistically and swallow failures.

Description: Uploads, checkouts and imports feel faster when people see the step and how many remain.
Do: Show 'Step 2 of 4' and a progress element with a label.
Don't: Hide the number of steps.

Description: A message that disappears in two seconds is gone before it is read, or before a screen reader finishes. Allow time and a way to dismiss.
Do: Show messages at least five seconds, pause on hover and focus, and keep them in a status region.
Don't: Use auto-dismiss under three seconds for anything important.

Description: People type phone numbers with spaces, dashes and brackets. Reject-on-format forces them to guess your rules.
Do: Normalise on the server and accept spaces, case and common separators.
Don't: Return an error because of a space.

Description: Autofill saves effort for people with motor or memory difficulties. The autocomplete attribute names the purpose so browsers can fill it.
Do: Add autocomplete tokens such as given-name, email, street-address, postal-code.
Don't: Turn autocomplete off on name and address fields.

Description: Slow connections tempt people to press twice, creating duplicate orders. Show progress and ignore repeat presses.
Do: Set aria-busy and a pending label on submit, and make the server idempotent.
Don't: Leave the button live while the request runs.

Description: Image puzzles block blind users and many with cognitive disabilities. Prefer invisible checks, and give a non-puzzle path if one is needed.
Do: Use server-side rate limits, honeypots or a challenge with an alternative.
Don't: Gate the form with a distorted-text puzzle.

Issue: Choose Radios Over Selects for Few Options
Description: With four or fewer options, radios show everything at a glance and take one click, where a select hides them behind two.
Do: Use radios for up to about five choices and a select beyond that.
Don't: Hide three options in a dropdown.

Description: A message that stays after the field is corrected tells users it still fails, and a screen reader keeps announcing it.
Do: Remove the message and aria-invalid as soon as the value passes.
Don't: Wait for the next submit to clear it.

Description: Within one process, asking for the same detail again, such as a billing address already given as delivery, costs time and errors.
Do: Prefill from earlier steps or offer a 'same as' checkbox.
Don't: Make users retype details they just entered.
Code Example Good: <label><input type='checkbox' checked> Billing same as delivery</label>

Issue: Do Not Disable Submit Up Front
Description: A greyed-out button gives no clue why it is off and is skipped by keyboard users. Let them press and explain what is missing.
Do: Keep the button enabled and show the error summary on submit.
Don't: Disable the button until every field looks valid.

Description: On a long form, errors below the fold go unseen. A summary at the top, moved to on submit, lists them with links to each field.
Do: After a failed submit, focus a summary with links to every invalid field.
Don't: Reload the page with errors scattered and focus on nothing.

Description: A form error message in text, beside the field, names which field failed and why. A red border alone says something is wrong and nothing more.
Do: Write an error message in text, adjacent to the field, naming the field.
Don't: Show a coloured outline or an icon only.
Code Example Good: Enter an email like name@example.com

Description: 'Invalid input' is no help. Say what is expected, or offer the likely correction when it is known.
Do: State the rule or the corrected value: what to type, not just what is wrong.
Don't: Show generic 'Something went wrong' messages.

Issue: Field Width Hints at the Answer
Description: A postcode field as wide as the page suggests a paragraph. Width cues the expected length.
Do: Size short fields (postcode, year, CVC) to fit their content.
Don't: Stretch every field to full width.

Description: A set of radios or checkboxes needs a shared question. fieldset and legend give screen readers that context.
Do: Wrap related choices in fieldset with a legend.
Don't: Put the question in a plain paragraph above the radios.

Description: Typing Japanese, Chinese or Korean uses a composition window where Enter confirms a character. Treating that Enter as submit sends half-typed text.
Do: Ignore Enter while event.isComposing is true.
Don't: Submit on every Enter keydown.

Issue: Keep Input After a Failed Submit
Description: Wiping a long form because one field failed is the quickest way to lose a customer.
Do: Re-render with the user's values and only mark the failing fields.
Don't: Reset the form or drop values on server error.

Description: People need to know what they must fill in before they try. Choose one convention and explain it.
Do: Use the required attribute, and say 'required' or '(optional)' in the label text.
Don't: Use a bare red asterisk with no key.

Description: The right keyboard cuts typing time on phones. Numeric codes, email addresses and search each have one.
Do: Set inputmode and enterkeyhint; use pattern for digit-only codes.
Don't: Show the full text keyboard for a six-digit code.

Description: Cancelling the paste event makes people retype long passwords and codes, and defeats password managers.
Do: Leave paste enabled on every field, including confirm-email.
Don't: Cancel the paste event on any field.

Description: Placeholder text has low default contrast and vanishes on input. It can show a format but never carry the instruction.
Do: Keep placeholder for a short example and put rules in help text under the label.
Don't: Hide the required format in a placeholder.

Issue: Review Before Legal or Money Commitments
Description: Payments, bookings and legal submissions need a way to check, correct or reverse before the final commitment.
Do: Show a review step with edit links and a clear final button that names the amount.
Don't: Charge on the same click that finishes the form.

Description: Typing blind on a phone keyboard is the top cause of failed sign-ups. A show/hide control lets people check what they typed.
Do: Add a toggle button with an accessible name and aria-pressed state.
Don't: Force a confirm-password field as the only check.

Description: Logins must not depend on remembering or transcribing a code, or solving a puzzle, without an alternative such as paste, password manager or a link.
Do: Allow paste, allow password managers, offer passkeys or email links.
Don't: Block paste in the password field or add a distorted-text puzzle.

Description: A screen reader only reads an error message beside a field if the two are linked. aria-describedby and aria-invalid connect them.
Do: Set aria-invalid='true' and aria-describedby pointing at the message id.
Don't: Place the message in the DOM with no link to the input.

Description: type=email, tel, url, number and date bring the right mobile keyboard and built-in checks. Wrong types make phone users hunt for the at sign.
Do: Choose the input type that matches the data; add inputmode for numeric codes.
Don't: Use type=text for everything.

Issue: Validate on Blur, Not on Every Key
Description: Showing 'invalid email' after the first letter is typed scolds people for being mid-sentence. Wait until they leave the field.
Do: Validate on blur or submit; once a field is invalid, re-check as they type.
Don't: Flag errors while the user is still typing.

Description: A placeholder disappears once someone types, and many readers treat it as pre-filled content. A persistent label tells people what each box wants.
Do: Put a label element above the field, connected by for and id.
Don't: Use the placeholder as the only label.

Description: Navigating away from a half-filled form without warning throws away work. Ask first, or save drafts.
Do: Listen for beforeunload only while the form is dirty.
Don't: Always show a leave prompt, even on clean forms.

Description: Without feedback, people press again. A pending label and busy state show the request is in flight.
Do: Change the label ('Saving'), set aria-busy, and keep the width stable.
Don't: Leave the button unchanged.

Description: A delete confirmation catches slips that cannot be undone. Name the item and the consequence in the dialog and on the button.
Do: Use a dialog that restates what will go and a button labelled Delete invoice.
Don't: Use OK and Cancel with a vague prompt.

Description: A disabled button leaves people unsure what to do. Where possible keep it focusable with aria-disabled and say what is missing.
Do: Use aria-disabled and a hint, or let it submit and report.
Don't: Grey out a button with no reason.

Issue: Hover Is Not the Only Cue
Description: Hover states help mouse users, but must be paired with focus and active states for keyboard and touch.
Do: Style :hover, :focus-visible and :active together.
Don't: Define a hover style only.

Issue: Pointer Cursor on Real Controls Only
Description: cursor:pointer signals clickable. Applying it to non-interactive cards or text misleads.
Do: Set cursor:pointer on links and buttons; leave static content alone.
Don't: Make an entire non-clickable card show a hand.

Description: For reversible actions, confirm dialogs interrupt every time. A short undo window is faster and safer.
Do: Apply the action and show an Undo in a status message for several seconds.
Don't: Ask 'Are you sure?' for archiving.

Description: A control that does not react on press feels broken. A short visual change confirms the input registered.
Do: Style :active with a small shift or tone change within 100ms.
Don't: Give no feedback until the action finishes.

Description: Disabling selection on content stops people copying addresses, codes and quotes.
Do: Disable user-select only on controls and drag handles.
Don't: Apply user-select:none to the page.

Description: A setting that takes effect immediately is a switch. role='switch' with aria-checked tells assistive tech so.
Do: Use input checkbox with role='switch' or a button with aria-checked.
Don't: Use a styled div with no state.

Issue: Whole Card Click Keeps One Link
Description: Making a whole card clickable with nested links yields duplicate tab stops. One real link stretched over the card is cleaner.
Do: Put one anchor on the heading and stretch its hit area with ::after.
Don't: Wrap the card in a link containing other links.

Issue: Cap Line Width, Not Page Width
Description: Edge-to-edge text on a wide monitor is hard to track. Limit the container for reading and let imagery go wider.
Do: Give text containers max-width near 65ch and centre them.
Don't: Let paragraphs span 1600px.

Issue: Grid and Flex Children Need min-width 0
Description: Flex and grid items default to min-width:auto, so a long child stretches the whole row. Set min-width:0 to let it shrink.
Do: Add min-width:0 to children that hold text, tables or code.
Don't: Clip with overflow hidden to hide the stretch.

Description: URLs, emails and long words in narrow columns burst out and force horizontal scroll.
Do: Use overflow-wrap:anywhere on user-generated content cells.
Don't: Assume content fits.

Description: overflow:hidden on a wrapper also cuts off focus rings and dropdowns that extend beyond its box.
Do: Use overflow:clip with padding, or add padding so rings fit inside.
Don't: Hide overflow on a card that contains buttons without room for outlines.

Description: Every band at the same height and padding reads as a template. Let content decide each section's size.
Do: Vary section density, width and alignment, based on what each says.
Don't: Stack identical full-width bands: heading, three cards, repeat.
Code Example Good: /* hero tall, proof dense, quote narrow */

Description: Images, ads and late content that push text down as they load cause misclicks and hurt Cumulative Layout Shift.
Do: Set width and height or aspect-ratio on media and reserve slots for embeds.
Don't: Let images load with no dimensions.

Description: Notches and home indicators overlap fixed bars on modern phones. env() gives the insets.
Do: Pad bottom bars with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) and use viewport-fit=cover.
Don't: Pin a tab bar flush to the screen edge.

Description: Spacing chosen per element gives a page that feels slightly off. A 4 or 8 pixel scale keeps rhythm.
Do: Use spacing tokens and keep related items closer than unrelated ones.
Don't: Set margins to arbitrary values like 13px and 27px.

Description: A parent with transform, opacity or filter creates a stacking context that traps children's z-index. This explains most 'why is it behind' bugs.
Do: Inspect parents when layering fails and move overlays to the top level with a portal or dialog.
Don't: Raise z-index on the child repeatedly.

Description: On phones, 100vh includes the hidden address bar, so full-height sections spill. dvh tracks the visible area.
Do: Use min-height:100dvh with a vh fallback.
Don't: Use 100vh for hero heights on mobile.

Description: Random z-index values escalate into 9999 wars. A short named scale keeps dropdowns, sticky bars, modals and toasts in order.
Do: Define 5 to 6 layer tokens and use only those.
Don't: Add a bigger number whenever something hides.

Description: A visitor with a van or a car needs directions in one tap. The address as text plus a maps link covers both.
Do: Write the full address in text and link it to a maps URL.
Don't: Show only an embedded map with no text.

Issue: One Clear Action Above the Fold
Description: A visitor deciding whether to call or book should see the one action straight away, in the first screen on a phone.
Do: Place one primary button or phone link in the hero and repeat it in the header.
Don't: Offer five equal buttons.

Issue: Phone Number Is a Tap-to-call Link
Description: Most local customers phone from a phone. A tel: link turns the number into one tap, and it can sit in the header.
Do: Wrap the number in a tel: link with the international format.
Don't: Print the number as plain text or an image.

Description: People hesitate when they cannot guess a cost. 'From' prices or typical ranges set expectations.
Do: State 'from' prices or a range and what affects them.
Don't: Hide all pricing behind 'contact us'.

Issue: Quote and Booking Forms Stay Short
Description: Quote forms with ten fields lose phone users. Ask for name, contact and the job, then follow up.
Do: Limit the first form to about four fields and a text box.
Don't: Ask for budgets, ratings and company size up front.

Description: Visitors want to know if you are open now. Hours in plain text with today's status save a call.
Do: List hours in text, and say 'Open until 5pm' using the visitor's date.
Don't: Put hours in an image or only in a footer.

Description: Accreditations, insurance and review counts should be checkable. Link to the register or review page.
Do: Link each badge to its public register entry.
Don't: Show badges with no source.

Description: Fly-to animations over long distances can trigger dizziness. Jump or fade when reduced motion is set.
Do: Check prefers-reduced-motion and use jumpTo.
Don't: Always fly the camera.

Description: Hundreds of overlapping markers freeze phones and hide each other. Clusters expand on zoom.
Do: Group points beyond a density threshold into clusters.
Don't: Draw thousands of DOM markers.

Description: Map tiles and data from OpenStreetMap and others carry licence terms that require visible credit. Hiding it breaches the licence.
Do: Keep the attribution control visible and linked on every map.
Don't: Remove the attribution to tidy the corner.

Issue: Do Not Use Colour Alone on Maps
Description: Red and green pins cannot be told apart by many users. Differ by shape, label or icon.
Do: Vary marker shape or add short labels.
Don't: Use only hue to encode categories.

Description: Popups that insert user text as HTML allow script injection. Set text, not markup.
Do: Build popup content with textContent or sanitise first.
Don't: Interpolate unescaped strings into innerHTML.

Issue: Give a Text Alternative to the Map
Description: A map image is invisible to a screen reader. The address, directions and key points should also exist as text.
Do: Print the address and a short route description beside the map.
Don't: Present a location only as an embedded map.

Description: Pushing a 50 MB GeoJSON to the browser is slow. Tiles send only what the viewport needs.
Do: Serve large layers as vector tiles.
Don't: Load one huge GeoJSON.

Description: Panning and zooming by drag excludes keyboard and switch users. Arrow keys and zoom buttons must work.
Do: Enable keyboard handlers and visible zoom controls.
Don't: Disable keyboard and button controls.

Description: Counts per region follow population, so a big region always looks worst. Use rates or per-capita figures.
Do: Map rates per 1,000 people, and state the base in the legend.
Don't: Colour raw counts.

Description: Rainbow scales distort perceived differences. Sequential single-hue or ColorBrewer ramps read correctly and are safer for colour blindness.
Do: Use sequential ramps for ordered data and diverging for a midpoint.
Don't: Use a rainbow scale.

Description: A chart image or canvas is opaque to assistive tech. Offer a summary and the data in a table.
Do: Add a short text summary and a data table.
Don't: Ship a chart as a bare image.

Description: Maps, videos and widgets pop in and push content down. A fixed aspect ratio box prevents it.
Do: Wrap embeds in a box with aspect-ratio.
Don't: Let iframes resize themselves.

Description: Custom players often lose keyboard support. Native controls provide it by default.
Do: Use the native controls attribute or follow a tested player.
Don't: Hide controls and use a click-only overlay.

Issue: Anchor Jumps Land Below Fixed Bars
Description: In-page links that scroll a heading under a pinned header hide it. scroll-margin on targets fixes it.
Do: Set scroll-margin-top on anchored headings equal to header height.
Don't: Scroll with JavaScript offsets that break on zoom.

Description: People expect Back to undo the last navigation. Replacing history on every filter click or trapping it breaks that.
Do: Push history entries for meaningful state changes and avoid replaceState loops.
Don't: Rewrite history on each interaction.

Description: A breadcrumb trail helps when pages sit three or more levels down. On a flat five-page site it is clutter and fits our lint of decoration.
Do: Use a nav with aria-label='Breadcrumb' and an ordered list; skip it on one-level sites.
Don't: Add breadcrumbs to a site with one level.

Description: Seven or more top-level items bury what matters. Group and trim, and place the key action as a distinct button.
Do: Limit the top bar to about five links plus one action, and move the rest into the footer.
Don't: List every page in the header.

Description: Anchors take you somewhere and support open-in-new-tab; buttons do something on the page. Mixing them breaks middle-click and screen reader expectations.
Do: Use a with href for navigation and button for actions.
Don't: Use a with href='#' and a click handler as a button.

Description: Visitors click the logo to get back. It should link to the home page and carry an accessible name.
Do: Wrap the logo in a link to / with alt that names the business.
Don't: Leave the logo as an unlinked image.

Description: People scan a menu for 'you are here'. Colour alone fails some users, so expose the state to assistive tech too.
Do: Set aria-current='page' on the matching link and style it with weight or an underline as well as colour.
Don't: Highlight with colour only, or leave all links identical.

Issue: Mobile Menu Is a Real Disclosure
Description: A hamburger that toggles a menu should say whether it is open, be keyboard operable and close on Escape.
Do: Use a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; close on Escape and outside click.
Don't: Use a div icon that toggles a class.

Issue: Open in New Tab Only With Warning
Description: Opening a new window without saying so confuses people who use a screen reader and breaks Back. Offer it only when it helps and say so.
Do: Add 'opens in new tab' text and rel='noopener'.
Don't: Open external links in a new tab silently.

Description: A long list with only 'Next' leaves people lost. Show page numbers or a count, and label the nav.
Do: Use nav aria-label='Pagination' with aria-current on the current page and a total count.
Don't: Offer infinite scroll with no footer reach.

Description: Animated scrolling can disorient people with vestibular conditions. Apply it only when they have not asked for less motion.
Do: Set scroll-behavior:smooth inside a no-preference media query.
Don't: Force smooth scroll on html for everyone.

Description: Filters, tabs and search terms in the URL let people share, bookmark and return to a view. State kept in memory is lost on refresh.
Do: Reflect filters, sort and page in the query string.
Don't: Keep selected filters only in component state.

Description: A tall pinned header eats a phone screen and can cover focused items. Keep it short and reserve space for anchors.
Do: Cap a sticky header near 56 to 72px and set scroll-padding-top to match.
Don't: Pin a 140px header with a banner under it.

Description: Tabs use arrow keys between tabs and Tab into the panel. Plain links styled as tabs do not behave this way.
Do: Use role=tablist, tab, tabpanel with roving tabindex, or use real links if each tab is a page.
Don't: Build tabs from divs with click only.

Issue: Ask Only What You Need Now
Description: Long sign-ups cause drop-off. Ask for the minimum, and collect extras once the value is clear.
Do: Request email first, add profile fields later.
Don't: Demand twelve fields before use.

Description: Forced tours annoy returning users. Allow skip and make help reachable again.
Do: Provide Skip and a 'Show tips' option in settings.
Don't: Block use until a tour finishes.

Description: Chat widgets, tag managers and trackers add weight and block interaction. Each one needs a reason.
Do: Load third-party code after interaction or idle and remove unused tags.
Don't: Add every vendor's snippet in the head.

Description: Reading layout (offsetHeight) then writing styles in a loop forces repeated reflow.
Do: Batch reads, then writes.
Don't: Interleave reads and writes.

Description: Hashed filenames can be cached for a year, so repeat visits cost nothing.
Do: Send Cache-Control with immutable and a long max-age on hashed assets.
Don't: Serve assets with no cache headers.

Description: Background video can weigh tens of megabytes. A poster image and compressed formats load faster.
Do: Set preload='none' with a poster and offer reasonable bitrates.
Don't: Autoload full-size video on mobile.

Description: Scripts that block parsing delay first paint. defer and type=module run after the HTML is parsed.
Do: Use defer or module for scripts and split large bundles by route.
Don't: Put large scripts in the head without defer.

Description: Web fonts block text rendering unless told otherwise. font-display:swap shows a fallback immediately.
Do: Use font-display:swap or optional, preload the main face and subset the file.
Don't: Wait invisibly for the font.

Description: Interaction to Next Paint tracks how soon the page reacts to taps and keys. Long tasks on the main thread cause lag.
Do: Break up long JavaScript tasks and move heavy work off the main thread.
Don't: Run big loops inside click handlers.

Description: loading='lazy' saves data for images that may never be seen, but delays ones in the first view.
Do: Lazy-load images below the first screen; never the main one.
Don't: Lazy-load the hero image.

Description: Each weight and style is another file. Two or three is usually enough for a site.
Do: Load only weights used and prefer a variable font.
Don't: Load every weight of a family.

Description: Largest Contentful Paint measures when the main image or heading appears. fetchpriority and preloading speed it up.
Do: Add fetchpriority='high' to the hero image and preload its font.
Don't: Wait for JavaScript to inject the hero.

Description: A 4000px photo in a 400px slot wastes bandwidth. srcset and sizes let the browser pick.
Do: Provide srcset with widths and a sizes hint; use AVIF or WebP.
Don't: Ship the camera original.

Description: Smaller text forces zooming on phones and iOS zooms into inputs below 16px.
Do: Set the base size to 1rem or larger and inputs to 16px.
Don't: Set 12px body text.

Description: A breakpoint belongs where the layout breaks, not at a device width. Resize the window and add one where lines get too long.
Do: Set breakpoints where content needs them, in rem.
Don't: Chase iPhone widths.

Description: A card in a sidebar and in a main column needs different layouts at the same viewport width. Container queries style by the container.
Do: Use container-type:inline-size and @container rules.
Don't: Fake it with viewport media queries.

Description: A wide landscape crop becomes a speck on a phone. picture lets you serve a tighter crop.
Do: Use picture with media sources, and object-position to keep the subject.
Don't: Scale the wide image down.

Description: Most local-service visitors arrive on a phone. Starting from the narrow layout makes you choose what matters.
Do: Write base styles for small screens and add min-width queries as content needs.
Don't: Design only for a desktop mockup.

Description: A dropdown that opens on hover can not be opened on touch. Use click or focus-within as well.
Do: Open menus on click or focus; hover is an extra.
Don't: Hide submenus until hover.

Description: Sideways scrolling on a phone is a sign of a fixed-width element. Find the offender and fix it.
Do: Check at 320px; use max-width:100% on media and wrap tables in a scroll region.
Don't: Hide it with overflow-x:hidden on body.

Description: Wide tables break narrow screens. Allow the table's region to scroll, labelled and focusable.
Do: Wrap in a region with overflow-x:auto, tabindex='0' and a label.
Don't: Shrink text until it fits.

Description: Without a viewport tag, phones render a desktop-width page scaled down and the layout never responds.
Do: Include width=device-width, initial-scale=1 in the head.
Don't: Omit the tag.

Description: Suggestions need combobox semantics so screen readers can hear options and arrow keys can pick them.
Do: Follow the ARIA combobox pattern with aria-activedescendant.
Don't: Show a plain list of divs.

Description: '0 results' is a dead end. Suggest spelling fixes, broader terms or popular items.
Do: Say what was searched, offer alternatives and a contact route.
Don't: Show a blank page.
Code Example Good: No matches for 'boilr'. Try 'boiler' or call us.

Description: On sites with many pages, search should be one click away in a consistent place, inside a search landmark.
Do: Use role='search' with a labelled input.
Don't: Hide search in a menu.

Description: Sudden sign-out on a form wastes work. Warn before, and return people to where they were afterwards.
Do: Show a countdown prompt and keep state through re-login.
Don't: Redirect silently to the login page.

Issue: Mask Sensitive Values With a Reveal
Description: Card numbers and tokens shown in full are visible to shoulder surfers. Mask by default and let the user reveal.
Do: Show the last four digits and a reveal control.
Don't: Print full numbers in lists.

Description: Password managers need the right autocomplete tokens and standard fields. Breaking them pushes people to weak, reused passwords.
Do: Use autocomplete='current-password' and 'new-password' and a normal form.
Don't: Randomise field names or block autofill.

Description: Eye-and-pinch input is less precise than a mouse. Targets need to be large with clear hover feedback.
Do: Use at least 60pt targets and highlight on gaze.
Don't: Pack small controls tight.

Description: Too many depth layers cause eye strain. Keep key content on one plane and use depth for hierarchy.
Do: Limit depth to two or three layers and keep text on a flat plane.
Don't: Stack ornaments and floating panels.

Description: Autoplaying video burns data and battery and distracts. Let visitors start it.
Do: Show a poster and a play button; honour prefers-reduced-data where possible.
Don't: Autoplay a looping background clip.

Description: A page weight target, such as under 1 MB for a brochure site, forces choices that help every visitor on a slow connection.
Do: Set a budget per page and check it in the build.
Don't: Ignore weight until launch.

Description: The OS reserves edge swipes for back and home. A carousel or drawer that needs the same swipe will fight it.
Do: Keep custom swipes away from the screen edge and give buttons as an alternative.
Don't: Hijack the left edge swipe.

Description: Vibration confirms an action for some people, but it is unsupported on many devices and annoying when overused.
Do: Feature-detect navigator.vibrate and use it only for key confirmations.
Don't: Rely on vibration as the only feedback.

Issue: Hover Effects Do Not Hide Information
Description: Touch devices have no hover, so content revealed only on hover is unreachable. Gate hover styling by capability.
Do: Use @media (hover:hover) for hover polish and show the content by default.
Don't: Reveal prices or menus only on hover.

Issue: Long Press Needs a Visible Alternative
Description: Hidden long-press menus are undiscoverable. Offer the same options in a visible overflow menu.
Do: Expose the same actions through a labelled menu button.
Don't: Offer an action only on long press.

Issue: Place Key Actions Within Thumb Reach
Description: On large phones the top corners are hard to reach one-handed. Primary actions fit better in the lower half.
Do: Put the main action in a bottom bar or lower section.
Don't: Hide the main action in the top corner.

Issue: Pull to Refresh Does Not Fight Scroll
Description: Custom pull gestures can collide with the browser's own refresh. Limit them to lists where it makes sense and keep a visible refresh button.
Do: Use overscroll-behavior to manage chaining and offer a button.
Don't: Reimplement refresh on the whole page.

Description: Older mobile browsers waited before treating a tap as a click. touch-action:manipulation disables double-tap zoom on controls and removes the delay.
Do: Apply touch-action:manipulation to buttons and links.
Don't: Add a fast-click library.

Description: Adjacent small buttons invite the wrong tap. Gaps of 8px or more reduce errors.
Do: Leave at least 8px between touch targets.
Don't: Pack actions into a dense row.

Description: Fingertips are around 10 mm wide. Apple and Material both recommend about 44pt or 48dp targets; below that, mis-taps rise.
Do: Make tappable areas at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels, using padding if the icon is small.
Don't: Rely on 16px icons as the hit area.

Description: A modular scale of five or six sizes creates hierarchy. Many in-between sizes flatten it.
Do: Define sizes as tokens, with clear steps between heading levels.
Don't: Pick sizes ad hoc until headings and body are similar.

Description: text-wrap:balance evens line lengths so headings avoid a single orphan word on the last line.
Do: Apply text-wrap:balance to headings and pretty to paragraphs.
Don't: Insert manual line breaks.

Description: A fallback with different proportions makes text jump when the web font arrives. size-adjust and ascent overrides limit the shift.
Do: Declare a fallback @font-face with size-adjust.
Don't: Switch from Arial to a very different face.

Description: Justified text without hyphenation leaves rivers of white space, hard for dyslexic readers.
Do: Left-align body text; justify only with hyphens:auto in wide columns.
Don't: Justify narrow columns.

Description: Cramped lines tire the eye and fail the text-spacing test. Body text reads best near 1.5.
Do: Set unitless line-height 1.5 for body, 1.1 to 1.25 for large headings.
Don't: Use one tight line-height for all text.

Description: Short lines break rhythm; long lines make people lose their place.
Do: Use max-width in ch units on paragraph containers.
Don't: Let text run full width.

Issue: Monospace Is for Code and Data
Description: A monospace body face reads as costume and is slow for paragraphs. Use it for code, numbers and tables.
Do: Set code and tabular data in monospace; text in a text face.
Don't: Use monospace for brand voice.

Description: All caps slows reading and screen readers may spell abbreviations. Reserve it for short labels, and our lint avoids small uppercase labels above every heading.
Do: Write in sentence case; use capitals for one-word tags at most.
Don't: Set paragraphs or subtitles in uppercase.

Description: Proportional digits make columns of prices wobble. tabular-nums aligns them.
Do: Set font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums on number columns.
Don't: Leave digits proportional in price tables.

Description: Hierarchy comes from contrast in size, weight and colour. Text at nearly the same size reads flat.
Do: Make each level distinct, with at least a 1.25 ratio.
Don't: Use one family at one weight for everything.

Issue: Avoid Gradient Text and Gradient Buttons
Description: Gradient fills on headings and primary buttons are a leading tell of generic design and often reduce contrast at the edges.
Do: Use one flat colour from the palette for text and actions.
Don't: Fill headings with purple-to-blue gradients.

Description: Cards inside cards, or borders around every block, flatten hierarchy and look templated.
Do: Separate groups with space and one container level.
Don't: Wrap each block in a bordered rounded card.

Description: A hero with a generic gradient or stock figure says nothing about the business. A photo of the work, product or place does.
Do: Use an original photo of the work, or type alone.
Don't: Use abstract blobs or stock laptop images.

Issue: Icon Cards Are Not a Layout
Description: Three identical icon cards in a row say little. Content of unequal weight should look unequal.
Do: Pick one main point and give it room; support with plain text.
Don't: Repeat icon, title, blurb three times.

Issue: Skip the Eyebrow on Every Heading
Description: A tiny uppercase label above every section title repeats and adds noise; use one only where it adds meaning.
Do: Write a clear heading; add a label only when it names a category.
Don't: Put a small caps label above each h2.
